title: Odisha Pattachitra
description: Pattachitra is a 1,000-year-old painting tradition of Odisha, born as ritual cloth offerings (patta) in the service of Lord Jagannath of Puri. The word itself — pata (cloth) + chitra (picture) — describes canvases prepared from cotton cloth soaked in tamarind seed adhesive, coated with chalk and conch-shell powder, burnished to a soft ivory sheen, then painted stroke-by-stroke with mineral and vegetable pigments before a final lacquer seal. The craft is a tantric-pictorial grammar: every line, palette and border carries iconographic meaning rooted in the Jagannath temple canon.
technique_breakdown: 1. CLOTH PREPARATION — Fine cotton is soaked overnight in tamarind seed paste (Imli ka Chika), stretched, and dried. 2. GROUND — Several coats of chalk (Khadi Muti) mixed with conch-shell powder (Sankha) are applied and polished with stone burnishers to create the ivory surface. 3. OUTLINING — The master (gurumahapatra) sketches composition with thin paint brushes (kachipa), fixing borders and iconometry. 4. PIGMENTS — Natural mineral and vegetable colours: lamp black, orpiment yellow, Hingula (cinnabar red), indigo, and green from leaves; only one brush per colour. 5. FINISH — A lacquer coat of ground tamarind seed seals and deepens the pigments; fine work may then be detailed with a bamboo stylus (kamani).
